themes_detail.label: Tree emergency in Crown Heights
themes_detail.summary: Overgrown tree/branch complaints spiked to 15 THIS WEEK versus 0.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (2300% increase, z-score: 20.65), with concurrent spikes in dead/dying tree complaints (3 THIS WEEK vs 0.1 avg) and illegal tree damage reports (9 last week vs 2.0 avg), suggesting widespread arboreal infrastructure failure or storm damage requiring urgent Parks Department response.
evidence: Overgrown tree/branch complaints: 15 THIS WEEK vs 0.6 weekly average (z-score: 20.65, 2300% spike)
Dead/dying tree complaints: 3 THIS WEEK vs 0.1 weekly average (z-score: 8.69, 2300% spike)
Illegal tree damage complaints: 9 last week vs 2.0 weekly average (z-score: 4.04, 350% spike)
CB budget data shows recurring 'reconstruct or upgrade building in a park' requests, indicating long-deferred Parks infrastructure issues
reporting_angles: Canvass affected blocks in Prospect Heights and Crown Heights to identify what triggered the spike—recent storm, deferred maintenance, or contractor damage
Interview Parks Department about response timeline and whether they have adequate staffing (CB budget consistently requests more resources)

themes_detail.label: Homeless services capacity crisis
themes_detail.summary: Homeless person assistance complaints jumped to 22 TWO WEEKS AGO versus 3.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (577% spike, z-score: 8.44), signaling either a localized encampment or service gap; this aligns with repeated CB budget requests for homeless facilities and street outreach expansion, suggesting systemic undersourcing.
evidence: Homeless person assistance complaints: 22 two weeks ago vs 3.2 weekly average (z-score: 8.44, 577% spike)
CB repeatedly budgets for 'expand street outreach' and 'other facilities for homeless requests' year after year, indicating unmet need
Dead animal complaints also spiked 264% (5 complaints 2 weeks ago vs 1.4 avg), possible correlate to encampment conditions
reporting_angles: Map the 22 homeless assistance complaints to identify whether they cluster around specific parks, blocks, or transit hubs
Interview DHS and community leaders on whether a particular encampment emerged or service closures occurred 2-3 weeks prior

themes_detail.label: Lead hazard spike in housing stock
themes_detail.summary: Lead complaints increased to 10 LAST WEEK versus 4.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (142% spike, z-score: 3.21), coinciding with 273 alteration permits filed in the past 90 days; this suggests renovation-triggered lead disclosure or remediation failures in aging housing stock, with potential child health implications.
evidence: Lead complaints: 10 last week vs 4.1 weekly average (z-score: 3.21, 142% spike)
466 total DOB building permits filed in last 90 days, with 273 alterations (58% of filings), likely exposing lead in pre-1978 housing
CB budget requests consistently for 'assign additional building inspectors' and 'expand training programs,' indicating enforcement gaps
reporting_angles: Audit DOB inspection records: are lead violations being flagged during the 273 active alterations, and is compliance being enforced?
Interview families with young children in buildings that filed alteration permits; check health department for pediatric lead exposure reports

themes_detail.label: Food establishment safety deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Food establishment complaints surged to 8 TWO WEEKS AGO versus 2.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (205% spike, z-score: 3.41), suggesting either a localized outbreak or pattern of health code violations in restaurants or food service operations in the district.
evidence: Food establishment complaints: 8 two weeks ago vs 2.6 weekly average (z-score: 3.41, 205% spike)
No recent community board or council escalations logged, limiting corroboration
Pattern timing suggests potential seasonal or event-driven factor (weekend outbreaks, new vendor activity)
reporting_angles: Cross-reference the 8 complaints with DOHMH inspection records to identify which establishments and what violations
Identify if complaints cluster around a food court, market, or specific neighborhood commercial corridor

themes_detail.label: Building maintenance and facility failures
themes_detail.summary: Maintenance and facility complaints jumped to 19 LAST WEEK versus 4.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (375% spike, z-score: 8.02), potentially indicating accelerated public building deterioration or school facility issues across the district.
evidence: Maintenance/facility complaints: 19 last week vs 4.0 weekly average (z-score: 8.02, 375% spike)
CB budget requests for 'reconstruct or upgrade building in a park' and 'park, building, or access improvements' repeat annually
No specific facility name or type tagged to complaints in available data
reporting_angles: File FOIL request to identify which city-owned or managed facilities (schools, community centers, parks buildings) generated the 19 complaints
Visit facilities identified in complaints and document deferred maintenance patterns
